title: FAR Module 3 · TBS 2

fields.label: 3. Net Deferred Tax Asset After Valuation Allowance
4. Net Deferred Tax Position (Enter Net Liability Amount)

html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Deferred Tax Analysis

Calculate deferred tax assets and liabilities and determine the net amount after considering a valuation allowance.

Scenario

Apex Corp. has the following temporary differences at December 31.

Depreciation Difference $120,000 Future Taxable Amount
Warranty Liability $60,000 Future Deductible Amount
Accrued Compensation $40,000 Future Deductible Amount

The enacted tax rate expected when these temporary differences reverse is 25%.

Based on available evidence, Apex determines that a $5,000 valuation allowance is required against its deferred tax assets.

Required

1. Deferred Tax Liability
2. Gross Deferred Tax Asset
3. Net Deferred Tax Asset After Valuation Allowance
4. Net Deferred Tax Position (Enter Net Liability Amount)
explanation:
Step 1 — Deferred Tax Liability

The $120,000 depreciation difference creates future taxable amounts.

$120,000 × 25% = $30,000 DTL

Step 2 — Gross Deferred Tax Asset

Future deductible amounts total:

Warranty $60,000 + Accrued Compensation $40,000 = $100,000
$100,000 × 25% = $25,000 Gross DTA

Step 3 — Valuation Allowance

Gross DTA $25,000 − Valuation Allowance $5,000 = $20,000 Net DTA

Step 4 — Net Deferred Tax Position

DTL $30,000 − Net DTA $20,000 = $10,000 Net Deferred Tax Liability

CPA Takeaway

  • Future taxable amounts create DTLs.
  • Future deductible amounts create DTAs.
  • A valuation allowance reduces the deferred tax asset expected to be realized.
  • Netting depends on applicable tax jurisdiction and classification rules, but this simulation focuses on the arithmetic relationship among the balances.
